newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares soften early on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares soften early on profit taking.

text.p: Singapore shares eased slightly on Tuesday under profit-taking pressures, dealers said.
"It's been an uneventful start with investors uninspired to do anything," one remisier said.
Broad-based institutional selling of blue chips continued to be a drag on sentiment with the blip in counters late on Monday attributed to window-dressing.
At 0200 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 7.23 points to 1,980.72.
Volume was a meager 26 million lots with losing issues ahead of advancing ones 59 to 46.
Profit taking also hit smaller capitalisation issues and China-linked stocks, which had benefited previously from the handover euphoria.
Hogging the actives for a second day was Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical at US$1.13, down two cents.
Funds resumed their selling of blue chips such as F&N, dropping to S$9.95 down 25 cents, and Cycle & Carriage to S$14.70, down 10 cents.
Dealers said selling of Malaysian Multi-Purpose due to said fund switching on Monday susbsided. The issue was at S$2.05, up three cents.
